review_scope: static: retail instructions and emitted candidate listing

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: 104 bytes, 45 instructions, one block, zero edges; candidate 1/0, score 1.000.

checks.name: cfg_match
checks.rationale: Both decoders and the candidate report 1/0; retail has no branch in this routine.

checks.name: call_order
checks.rationale: strlen -> Mem_Alloc(length+0x1C, 4) -> 0x1C-byte header clear -> next/link_04 zero stores -> HeapList_Insert(&g_943970, record) -> name pointer at +0x08 -> strlen again -> name copy -> return record. Every step is in retail's order, including the redundant second strlen and the repeated zero stores.

checks.name: storage
checks.rationale: The record layout and head word are shared with native_4b1a90.cpp through loaded_file_record.hpp, which removed the duplicate definition that would otherwise have been an ODR violation.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Returns the record; retail has no failure branch when Mem_Alloc returns null and none was invented.

limitations: GCC inlines the header clear and calls CRT strlen/memcpy where retail uses rep sequences, so the candidate is 145 bytes against 104 with the same call order and block count.
Retail dereferences the allocation result with no null check; the transcription does the same and therefore crashes if Mem_Alloc fails, which is retail behaviour rather than a guard I added.
